threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line' and look baffled when locals refer to the 'food scene' without mentioning the market.
Caught a guy singing opera on the 59 last night. Sounded like a proper show, but the only audience were a couple of bemused drunks.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy in full lederhosen casually chatting with a busker wearing a beret outside Reuterplatz during a summer festival.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a 24-hour kebab shop next to a vintage vinyl store, both buzzing with a line out the door at 3 AM.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission if they still call it ‘the BART’ and know the quickest routes around all the construction traffic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading passengers on the 47 bus yesterday. Everyone was annoyed until he pulled out a sax. All of a sudden, we were in a jazz club.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists seem to think all bars serve tapas like they do in the guidebooks. In Gràcia, some spots serve only vermut and no food at all. Just drink and chat!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll catch them fumbling with the metro map, eyes darting around like a tourist, and always standing on the left side of the escalator.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 'vintage' shops in Dalston are a hidden gem, but the locals know they’re just overpriced thrift stores now.
Caught a guy on the 59 last night arguing with his own reflection in the window. Had to stifle a laugh. Brixton’s night vibes are wild.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street artist serenading a crowd of kids as they chased the pigeons—just a regular Tuesday afternoon in the park.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a late-night döner while listening to a spontaneous live street performance. It's like the city hums a different tune every night.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their nonchalant reaction to a BART train fire; they just keep sipping their coffee while the tourists panic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy calmly reading a book on the bus while the driver was yelling at a pigeon that wouldn’t move. Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about tapas and nightlife. Spend a Sunday morning here, and you’ll see locals enjoying their gardens and quiet moments.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their fresh excitement at ordering a 'café con leche' – locals just call it a 'café'.
